_comment: Capability -> component sets, read by sgs-init.mjs (--with) and by the app-start skill's interview. `core` is copied into every app unconditionally: it is the boot path (app-shell), the contracts (tokens, framework), the pieces the shell imports on every start, and `workflow` (the vocabulary and the three skills an app needs to reason about its own version). Each capability lists EVERY component it needs, so resolving a capability is a set-union, never a graph walk. A component may appear under several capabilities (swatch, field-badge); the union dedupes. Because a component carries its own SKILL.md, choosing a capability also decides which instructions land in the app - there is no separate skills list to keep in step. Removing a capability's WIRING from main.js and index.html is agent work the app-start skill owns; this file only decides which files exist.

layer-panel.asks: A left panel with layer rows (visibility, swatch, zoom-to)?

table._comment: `panel` is here because table.js IMPORTS foldPanel/isPanelFolded from it: the table folds the layer panel out of its way as it rises. An app that took the table without the layer panel previously scaffolded a table.js whose import target did not exist, and failed at first paint. Listing every component a capability needs, rather than the ones it feels like it owns, is what this file's set-union rule is for.
